an3.1:2.2: _Upaddava_ originally meant “rush to” (a ritual, Rig Veda 1.2.5, 8.5.7), as wild beasts fleeing for shelter (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 2.9.7). In the Suttas, the past participle _upadduta_ still conveys the sense of “rushed upon, harried”, but the noun form means “debacle”.
an3.1:2.3: For _upasagga_, at [pli-tv-kd1:20.20.2]() a brother fears a “catastrophic” flood has befallen his brother.
